x: Angela Patten and Gail Richardson covered the throws between them leaving Jacqui Smiter to fill in all the gaps. The two "J's", Georgina and Angela finally managed to compete in both relays with about 10-15 minutes rest.

Gail Richardson was pleased with her javelin win and although Julia Cockram must have been just as happy with her maximum score in the high jump, there is surely a more enjoyable way to spend an afternoon than Fosbury flopping onto one's back into a three inch deep puddle in the middle of the landing bed.

Best events for the seniors were the long and high jumps where the pairings of Andrea Abrams and Syreeta Stracey, and Julia Cockram and Laura Wilson both scored double wins, but the most surprising event was the 400 metre hurdles - when was the last time you saw Gail Richardson line up for the start of such a race?

It all went well from the very beginning thanks to double wins in the hammer with Gail Richardson getting pretty close to Pet Keeler. Michelle Stock won her first ever senior discus competition (not bad for someone who reached her 15th birthday just a couple of weeks earlier) and with another double…
To see Gail Richardson hurdling at Wimbledon Park you wouldn't have thought that she normally throws javelin and shot - and started off as a walker!
Andrea Abrams was not far short of her best in winning the long jump and Gail Richardson had a great afternoon with 2nd in the hammer, 2nd in the 'B' hurdles and 1st in the 'B' javelin.
The meeting started well with Gail Richardson and Hazel Mead both sending the hammer out to near pb and pb distances and they then went on to pick up good points in other throws as well.
Gail Richardson started off her athletics as a walker but is now mostly to be seen in the throwing events where she's not too far behind Pet Keeler's Hammer Record.

At the Royal Navy track at Portsmouth our throwers were in good form with 16 year-old Michelle Stock winning the 'A' discus and 'B' shot, and Angela Patten and Gail Richardson also scoring good points.
Angela Patten and Gail Richardson put up their normal solid show in the field events and there was a very nice double win from Harriet Payne in the under 15 sprints.
